subject: HealthBridge compliance: Type II report request & assurance locker onboarding
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthBridge compliance follow-up — next steps and evidence path

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: HealthBridge wants confirmation that Redwood can meet HIPAA + SOC 2 Type II controls for your inference workload and provide read-only access to artifacts for your security team.
- Immediate asks from your side: SOC 2 Type II report (latest), an interim bridge letter if report is older than 12 months, and a vendor security questionnaire (DDQ).
- Our proposal: we can share the Type II summary and a draft bridge letter, then provision time-limited access to our Assurance Locker for artifact download (audit logs, policy excerpts).

Action items I committed to:
1) Send the DDQ template you mentioned and confirm playbook for artifact handoff (today).
2) Loop in Security/Trust to provision the Assurance Locker invite and generate a temporary bridge letter draft (EOD).
3) Share HubSpot deal and timeline so your procurement can coordinate any contracts.

Vanessa — I copied you to coordinate the locker invite and attach the assurance artifacts. Samantha — when you have a moment, confirm the preferred format for the DDQ (spreadsheet vs. portal form) and whether your legal team needs an NDA before we upload any sensitive attachments.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthbridge.com>

Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthBridge compliance follow-up — next steps and evidence path

Thanks Jonas — this is perfect. A couple quick answers: 

- DDQ: spreadsheet (XLSX) is best for our intake team.
- NDA: not required to start; we can accept redacted artifacts in the first pass.
- Bridge letter: we do need an attestation stating the scope (inference API only) and timeframe covered.

Two questions for Redwood Security: can you confirm whether logs for customer-specific requests are retained and for how long? Also, if you have a short summary of PII handling under our HIPAA scope that helps the reviewer.

I'll loop in procurement once I see the HubSpot link. Appreciate the fast move here.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of IT Security, HealthBridge

Thanks — Jonas

Thanks Jonas — quick update from Trust & Compliance ops (see attached artifacts):

1) Assurance Locker: created a time-limited read-only invite for security@healthbridge.com — link below (expires in 14 days). Permission is limited to the HealthBridge folder.
   - Invite: https://trust.redwood.ai/locker/invite?token=kb2-9x7s

2) Bridge letter: attached draft — redwood_assurance_bridgeletter_draft.pdf. It explicitly scopes coverage to "Redwood Inference hosted inference endpoints (inference.redwood.ai)" and references the 2027 SOC 2 Type II report. Please review the scope language; we can make it narrower if HealthBridge needs line-of-business constraints.

3) Type II report summary: soc2_typeII-summary-2027.pdf (attached). Full report access requires a completed DDQ and a signed NDA; however, per Jonas/Samantha we are providing a redacted summary and the bridge letter for initial review.

4) Log retention & HIPAA handling (one-paragraph): 
   - Retention: request-level telemetry and audit logs are retained for 180 days by default. Customers can opt into extended retention under Dedicated/Private plans. Request payloads are not stored persistently unless a customer enables logging for debugging.
   - HIPAA: Redwood maintains BA agreements, encrypts data in transit and at rest (AES-256), and isolates customer data in tenant-scoped buckets. Our processing flow minimizes storage of PHI; where PHI is processed, access is role-based and logged.

Next steps: Jonas — please share the DDQ that Samantha will complete. Once we receive the DDQ we can lift the redaction restriction and provide scoped report access (Trust & Compliance will require a quick attestation form).

Attachments (sent): redwood_assurance_bridgeletter_draft.pdf, soc2_typeII-summary-2027.pdf

—Marissa

Appreciate the team moving quickly.
